title: ClearPath — AI Document Intelligence Platform
short: An AI-powered document intelligence platform that processes complex official documents through an isolated Python/Docling OCR service and a hot-path 5-stage atomic preprocessing pipeline (chunking + embedding moved to a parallel background path), followed by a 5-stage LLM analysis pipeline — delivering plain-English summaries, tracked deadlines, and extracted action items via real-time SSE, with a 30–35% speedup and reduced memory footprint versus running every stage inline.
problem: Immigrants, refugees, and underserved communities struggle to understand complex official documents (notices, legal letters, benefit communications), risking missed deadlines and critical actions. Existing tools either hallucinate details or fail to provide legally grounded, actionable steps. Worse, a single mid-pipeline crash on a multi-minute analysis can leave users staring at a frozen UI with no way to recover.
process: Designed a robust monorepo architecture with a Next.js frontend, an Express/TypeScript backend orchestrating three concurrent Node processes (API, Dispatcher, Workers), and a separate Python/Docling OCR service for layout parsing

Split the analysis pipeline into 8 atomic preprocessing stages (initialization, OCR, cleaning, structuring, chunking, embedding, summarizing, completion) — each its own BullMQ job, every state change written to a transactional outbox, so any stage can crash and restart without losing progress

Refactored the hot path to 5 critical preprocessing stages (initialization → OCR → cleaning → structuring → completion) that block the user-visible result, and moved chunking + embedding to a parallel background path that runs on its own queue — the user gets the result 30–35% faster while the embedding model is loaded in a separate worker, dropping the hot-path memory footprint substantially

Isolated the Docling OCR stage on its own dedicated BullMQ queue (OCR_QUEUE_NAME) — the Python service and Node workers can never claim each other's jobs, and Node restarts don't disrupt OCR throughput

Implemented a reliable Outbox Dispatcher using PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY (instant) plus a polling fallback (every OUTBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) to guarantee BullMQ job delivery even if the dispatcher was down when NOTIFY fired

Built a two-phase pipeline featuring a human-in-the-loop 'Extraction Verification Gate' — the pipeline pauses after text extraction so the user can review/edit before any LLM tokens are spent, with PATCH /extracted-content auto-save and POST /confirm-extraction to resume

Implemented a 5-stage LLM pipeline (Understanding, Candidate Extraction, Grounding via Tavily, User-Facing Synthesis, Safety Review) utilizing Groq and Llama 3.3 70B, with strict Zod validation and a safe fallback for every stage so the pipeline never crashes on a malformed response

Integrated the Tavily Search API to cross-reference extracted facts against official .gov/.edu sources in real time, then forced the LLM's trusted_sources output to be a subset of the snippets Tavily actually returned — eliminating hallucinated URLs at the schema level
Developed a lossless Server-Sent Events streaming layer: Redis Pub/Sub for live updates + Postgres event log replay via Last-Event-ID, so a 2-second network blip never drops a pipeline event

Secured the platform with custom RS256 JWT in httpOnly cookies, argon2 password hashing, an internal API key guard for dispatcher endpoints, and a 3-layer prompt-injection defence (delimited untrusted input, explicit security warning in every system prompt, and forced ground-truth URLs)
outcome: Delivered a production-grade, fault-tolerant document intelligence platform that transforms high-stakes legal and official documents into accessible, verified, and actionable insights while keeping the user informed in real-time. The 5-stage hot path returns results 30–35% faster with a substantially smaller in-memory footprint, while chunking + embedding run in parallel on a dedicated background worker without blocking the user.

stats.architecture: 4-process backend (API, Outbox Dispatcher, BullMQ Workers, Python/Docling OCR)
stats.pipeline: 5-stage hot path (init → OCR → cleaning → structuring → completion) + parallel chunking/embedding background path + 5-stage LLM pipeline + Human-in-the-loop verification gate
stats.queues: Three isolated BullMQ queues (Node ANALYSIS_QUEUE_NAME hot path, Node BACKGROUND_QUEUE_NAME for chunking/embedding, Python OCR_QUEUE_NAME)
stats.performance: 30–35% faster time-to-result on the user-visible pipeline by moving chunking + embedding off the hot path (same output quality)
stats.memory: Significantly reduced hot-path memory footprint — the embedding model and chunker live in a separate background worker and no longer compete for memory with the result-producing stages
stats.realtime: Lossless SSE streaming via Postgres event replay + Redis Pub/Sub

caseStudy.tlDr: Architected and built ClearPath, an AI document intelligence platform designed to decode complex official documents. Engineered a highly reliable multi-process backend (Node API + Dispatcher + Workers + Python/Docling OCR) featuring a transactional outbox, three isolated BullMQ queues (hot path, background path, Python OCR), 8 atomic preprocessing stages with chunking + embedding moved off the user-visible hot path for a 30–35% speedup and reduced memory footprint, real-time lossless SSE updates, and a 5-stage LLM pipeline grounded in official .gov/.edu sources to prevent hallucinations.
caseStudy.problem: High-stakes documents like immigration notices or benefit letters are notoriously difficult to understand, especially for non-native speakers. A simple misunderstanding can lead to missed deadlines or legal peril. Standard LLM wrappers are too risky for this because they hallucinate facts and invent URLs. On top of accuracy, a multi-minute analysis pipeline must survive process crashes and network drops without losing state — and the user must be able to verify the extracted text before any LLM tokens are spent on it. Performance is also a feature: every stage that runs inline on the hot path is wall-clock time the user is waiting, and every model loaded in the hot-path worker is memory the result-producing stages have to fight for.
caseStudy.constraints: Zero tolerance for lost processing jobs if any process crashes mid-pipeline. Strict requirement for LLM accuracy/grounding — every trusted URL must come from a real Tavily search result. Protection against malicious prompt injections inside user-uploaded PDFs. Long-running multi-minute analyses that must stream real-time progress to the client and recover gracefully on reconnect. OCR is a Python service (Docling/RapidOCR); the Node worker and Python service must share one outbox without claiming each other's jobs. Hot-path performance and memory: chunking + embedding are necessary for retrieval quality but they were the slowest stages on the user-visible path, and loading the embedding model was a meaningful share of worker memory.
caseStudy.myRole: Full-Stack Engineer & AI Pipeline Architect — designed and implemented the monorepo, the 12-file database migration set, custom RS256 JWT auth, the Outbox Dispatcher, the three BullMQ queues (hot path, background, Python OCR), the Node worker orchestration, the Python/Docling OCR service, the SSE streaming layer, and the 5-stage AI pipeline.
responsibilities: Designed the full database schema in Supabase PostgreSQL — 12 SQL migrations covering users, documents, analysis requests, pipeline events, sections, chunks, facts, results, the outbox, RLS grants, and the AWAITING_VERIFICATION / AI_* enum extensions

Implemented the Outbox Dispatcher (src/outbox/dispatcher.ts) using PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY alongside a polling fallback, with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the outbox so multiple dispatcher instances never double-process

Refactored the pipeline into two parallel paths: a 5-stage hot path (stage-initialization → extract-layout-and-ocr → cleaning → structuring → completion) that the user is waiting on, and a background path (chunking + embedding) running on its own BullMQ queue — chunking and embedding are persisted to Postgres asynchronously and used for retrieval, while the user-visible result ships the moment the hot path completes, achieving a 30–35% speedup with the same output quality and a substantially reduced hot-path memory footprint

Split preprocessing into 8 atomic stages in total across both paths — every stage is its own BullMQ job, every transition writes a document_pipeline_outbox row in the same transaction as the state update, and isStageCompleteOrPast() guards keep retries idempotent across paths

Built the isolated Python/Docling OCR service (app/backend/services/ocr-engine/) — runs in its own process, consumes from a dedicated OCR_QUEUE_NAME, writes the document.extracted outbox event via Supabase, and never connects to the Node worker's queue

Constructed the 5-stage AI worker pipeline: Document Understanding, Candidate Extraction, Grounding & Verification (via Tavily restricted to .gov/.edu), User-Facing Synthesis, and Safety Review with both LLM-judged and rule-based guardrails

Engineered lossless SSE infrastructure: per-client Redis subscriber connections, Postgres event-log replay from Last-Event-ID on reconnect, periodic heartbeats, and an active /analysis/running-check session restore on page load so users can navigate away and back without losing their in-flight analysis

Implemented defensive LLM engineering — every stage validates with Zod, returns a safe fallback on failure (sets needs_human_review: true), enforces uncertainty language in the summary, normalises questions, and sanitises trusted_sources to URLs that actually appeared in the Tavily results

Secured auth end-to-end: RS256 JWT access + refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies, sid cookie for session tracking, argon2 password hashing, express-rate-limit on login and refresh, x-internal-api-key guard on the dispatcher endpoint

Developed the Next.js frontend with SWR caching, drag-and-drop file uploads, real-time SSE timeline feeds (via @microsoft/fetch-event-source), interactive extraction verification panels with auto-save, and a results view with saved/bookmarks, action-item toggles, and history filters
approach: Prioritize reliability: Use the outbox pattern so the database transaction and queue dispatch are fundamentally tied together — if the DB write commits, the job is guaranteed to be enqueued eventually, and if it doesn't commit, no job is enqueued

Atomicity over batching: every pipeline stage is a standalone BullMQ job that loads what it needs, does its work, writes an outbox event, and exits. This means any stage can crash, restart, or scale horizontally without losing pipeline state — state lives in Postgres, not in worker memory

Separate the hot path from the background path: not every stage is on the user's critical path. Chunking + embedding are necessary for retrieval but they were the slowest stages on the user-visible path — moving them to a parallel BullMQ queue (BACKGROUND_QUEUE_NAME) returned the user-visible result 30–35% faster and let the embedding model live in a separate worker that doesn't compete for memory with the result-producing stages

Isolate heterogeneous runtimes: the Python Docling OCR service runs in its own process on a dedicated BullMQ queue (OCR_QUEUE_NAME) so the Node worker and the Python service can never claim each other's jobs

Human-in-the-loop at the extraction gate: stop the pipeline after raw text extraction so the user can verify dates, contacts, and text before any LLM tokens are spent on analysis — supported by PATCH auto-save and POST confirm-extraction endpoints

Defensive LLM engineering: every pipeline stage has strict Zod schema validation and a safe fallback. The pipeline gracefully degrades (sets needs_human_review: true) rather than crashing, and every trusted URL in the final output is a subset of the URLs Tavily actually returned

Lossless real-time UX: combine Redis Pub/Sub for live updates with Postgres event-log replay via Last-Event-ID. A 2-second network blip must not drop a single pipeline event — and the client must auto-recover via an active session-restore on page load
technicalSolution: Backend: Express 4, Node.js, TypeScript, raw pg connection pool, Zod-validated env schema, Custom RS256 JWT Auth (argon2 + httpOnly cookies + sid session tracking)

OCR service: Python 3 + Docling + RapidOCR, isolated process under services/ocr-engine/, consuming from a dedicated BullMQ queue (OCR_QUEUE_NAME) and writing outbox events back to Postgres via the Supabase client

Queue & Workers: BullMQ backed by Redis (ioredis) — three separate queues: a Node ANALYSIS_QUEUE_NAME hot path (initialization → OCR → cleaning → structuring → completion), a Node BACKGROUND_QUEUE_NAME for chunking + embedding that runs in parallel without blocking the user, and a Python OCR_QUEUE_NAME — four separate ioredis connection factories (queue, worker, publisher, subscriber), exponential backoff retries, and idempotent job IDs derived from the analysis request

AI & Processing: Groq API (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) with a 25-second per-stage timeout, Tavily API restricted to .gov/.edu hostnames for grounding, askGroqJson() helper that strips markdown fences, finds the first {, and validates against the stage's Zod schema with a fallback on failure

Background path: chunking + embedding run on a dedicated worker process that loads the embedding model once and reuses it across jobs; chunks and embeddings are persisted to Postgres asynchronously and the hot path never waits on them — measured 30–35% faster time-to-result on the user-visible pipeline, with the same output quality

Real-time: @microsoft/fetch-event-source on the client communicating with custom SSE endpoints — per-client Redis subscribers, Postgres replay from Last-Event-ID on reconnect, periodic heartbeats, and an active /analysis/running-check session restore on page load

Frontend: Next.js 14 App Router, Tailwind CSS, SWR for caching, Framer Motion for timeline animations, drag-and-drop uploads, interactive extraction verification with auto-save, results panel with action-item toggles, bookmarks, and history filters

Data: Supabase Storage buckets (documents for raw uploads, parsed-documents for OCR Markdown output), Supabase Postgres for everything else with JSONB columns for extracted_content, outbox events, and pipeline result payloads
caseStudy.architectureNotes: ClearPath is an event-driven, decoupled, multi-runtime system with two parallel Node paths and one Python path. The Next.js frontend talks to the Express API for uploads, auth, confirm-extraction, history, and SSE. The API writes all state changes to Postgres in transactions that also INSERT into document_pipeline_outbox. The Outbox Dispatcher (separate process) subscribes to Postgres NOTIFY on outbox inserts and polls as a safety net, then enqueues the next stage's BullMQ job. Three queues exist: ANALYSIS_QUEUE_NAME (Node hot path: initialization → OCR → cleaning → structuring → completion), BACKGROUND_QUEUE_NAME (Node background path: chunking → embedding — runs in parallel, never blocks the user), and OCR_QUEUE_NAME (Python Docling). The Python OCR service writes its document.extracted outbox event via the Supabase client, so the same NOTIFY triggers the next Node stage regardless of which runtime wrote the row. Each worker stage persists its result and publishes progress to Redis Pub/Sub for live SSE clients while also writing a row to document_pipeline_events so reconnecting clients can replay from their Last-Event-ID. The API's SSE endpoint keeps one Redis subscriber per active client, replays any missed events from Postgres, and emits periodic heartbeats. Stage transitions are guarded by isStageCompleteOrPast() so BullMQ retries are idempotent. Idempotency on analyze requests is enforced both at the DB level (unique index on idempotency_key) and at the queue level (BullMQ job ID = analysis:<requestId>). The hot-path result ships the moment the completion stage fires, while the background path keeps running until chunks and embeddings land in Postgres for retrieval — net 30–35% faster time-to-result with the same output quality.

outcomes.qualitative: Achieved a highly resilient multi-runtime pipeline that survives process restarts and network drops without losing user documents or analysis states, successfully bridging the gap between raw, intimidating government notices and actionable, human-readable checklists. After moving chunking and embedding off the hot path, the user-visible result returned 30–35% faster with the same output quality, and the hot-path memory footprint dropped substantially because the embedding model and chunker live in a dedicated background worker — and all of it with a Python OCR service, a Node hot path, and a Node background path sharing one outbox without ever claiming each other's jobs.

proofPoints: Implemented a deterministic transactional outbox pattern via Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY + polling fallback, with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for safe horizontal dispatcher scaling

Split the pipeline into 8 atomic preprocessing stages + 5 LLM stages across three isolated BullMQ queues (hot path, background path, Python OCR) — every stage can crash and restart independently without losing state
Moved chunking + embedding off the user-visible hot path to a parallel background worker — measured 30–35% faster time-to-result on the user-visible pipeline with the same output quality
Reduced hot-path memory footprint by loading the embedding model and chunker in a separate worker process that no longer competes for memory with the result-producing stages
Isolated the Python/Docling OCR service on its own dedicated BullMQ queue (OCR_QUEUE_NAME) and shared a single outbox with the Node pipeline via the Postgres NOTIFY trigger
Built a lossless SSE layer that combines Redis Pub/Sub with Postgres event-log replay via Last-Event-ID plus an active session-restore on page load
Eliminated LLM hallucination risk by forcing every trusted_sources URL to be a subset of URLs Tavily actually returned from .gov/.edu searches
Built a pipeline that survives LLM schema failures by using graceful Zod fallbacks (every stage returns a safe default with needs_human_review: true)
Enforced a 3-layer prompt-injection defence: delimited untrusted input, explicit SECURITY WARNING in every system prompt, and ground-truth URL constraints
lessons: Atomicity beats batching for long pipelines. Splitting the work into small BullMQ jobs that each commit their own outbox event is what lets the system survive crashes — long-lived in-memory workers lose state on restart.

The outbox pattern is essential when combining Postgres with Redis queues. Direct enqueuing from API routes leads to race conditions and lost jobs; outbox + LISTEN/NOTIFY + polling fallback guarantees at-least-once delivery.

Separate the hot path from the background path. Not every stage is on the user's critical path. Moving chunking + embedding off the user-visible hot path returned the result 30–35% faster with the same output quality, and let the embedding model live in a separate worker that no longer fights for memory with the result-producing stages — the slow stages are still running, just not on the user's clock.

Isolate heterogeneous runtimes via dedicated queues. The Python Docling service and the Node workers share the same Postgres outbox but consume from separate BullMQ queues (OCR_QUEUE_NAME vs ANALYSIS_QUEUE_NAME) so they can never claim each other's jobs.

Model loading is a memory cost, not just a latency cost. Loading the embedding model inline on the hot path was a meaningful share of worker memory; isolating it to a dedicated background worker dropped the hot-path memory footprint substantially without any output change.

LLMs will fail validation eventually. Building pipeline stages with safe fallbacks (returning needs_human_review: true instead of crashing) is critical for production AI, especially on high-stakes documents.

Trust but verify at the schema level. Telling the LLM not to invent URLs is not enough — forcing trusted_sources to be a subset of the URLs Tavily actually returned turns prompt-engineering hope into a hard guarantee.

Real-time UX requires stateful backends. Relying strictly on live Pub/Sub means a 2-second client network blip loses pipeline events; storing events in Postgres and replaying via Last-Event-ID — plus an active session-restore on page load — makes reconnects invisible to the user.

A human-in-the-loop verification gate is worth the UX cost. Stopping the pipeline after OCR so the user can review extracted text before any LLM tokens are spent protects against OCR errors compounding into LLM hallucinations.
caseStudy.callToAction: Interested in seeing how to build resilient, fault-tolerant, multi-runtime AI pipelines with a hot path + background path split, human-in-the-loop verification, multi-queue outbox orchestration, and lossless real-time streaming? Review the architecture or reach out.

title: EconoQuest — AI Economics Simulator
role: Full-Stack Engineer, AI/RAG Architect & Simulation Designer
short: Govern a nation across 7–8 fiscal years, adjusting 8 real policy levers and watching 10 economic metrics respond — guided by a Socratic AI advisor powered by a full RAG pipeline, not generic hints.
problem: Economics education teaches consequences by description, not by experience. You can read that printing money causes inflation — but you don't feel it until you've made the choice yourself and watched your currency collapse two rounds later. EconoQuest was built to close that gap: compound causality you live with, not memorize.
process: Designed a 7–8 round simulation engine with 8 policy levers (tax, interest rates, spending, R&D, tariffs, money supply, foreign lending, wealth fund risk) mapping to 10 outcome metrics
Built a full RAG pipeline: game state embedded → pgvector retrieval from 99 knowledge chunks across 5 layers → Llama 3.3 70B via Groq streamed over WebSocket
Engineered a Fastify gateway handling cross-domain auth, same-domain cookie proxying, LRU caching keyed by state hash, and load balancing across two HuggingFace Spaces per service
Designed 99 game-situated RAG chunks (game mechanics, dangerous combos, crisis playbooks, round strategy, historical analogies — Weimar, Volcker, Singapore, Zimbabwe)
Built a pure-Python conflict detector that flags dangerous policy pairs before any LLM call — domain expertise as logic, not inference
Fixed a WebSocket streaming bug where Groq tokens arriving within the same millisecond collapsed React's batch buffer — solved by accumulating tokens via index ref, bypassing batching entirely
Designed a 7-archetype system and an AI-narrated mandate timeline review generated at game end
outcome: Submitted to Hackonomics 2026 — built entirely solo. Delivered a production-grade economics simulation with a full RAG pipeline, Socratic AI advisor, conflict detection system, real-time WebSocket streaming, and a competitive Hall of Fame — on zero cloud spend.

stats.infrastructure: 100% free — HuggingFace Spaces, Supabase, Groq, zero cloud spend
stats.build: Solo — simulation engine, RAG pipeline, gateway, streaming layer, frontend, deployment

caseStudy.tlDr: Built a browser-based economics simulation with a full RAG advisory pipeline, Socratic AI advisor, and real-time WebSocket streaming — solo, on free infrastructure, for Hackonomics 2026. Players govern a nation across 7–8 fiscal years, adjusting real policy levers and living with the compound consequences — guided by a Socratic AI that asks pointed questions using their actual numbers and never gives answers.
caseStudy.problem: Economics education describes consequences; it doesn't produce them. Reading about the Weimar Republic gives you a fact. Making a money-printing decision at round 3 and watching it compress real salaries by round 5 gives you intuition. EconoQuest was designed to be the second kind of learning — a simulation where early policy decisions constrain your options for years, and every outcome is traceable to a choice you made.
caseStudy.constraints: Free infrastructure only — no paid cloud, no paid ML APIs. Solo build. The Socratic constraint was technically the hardest: a capable model defaults to being helpful, and helpful usually means giving the answer. Getting Llama 3.3 70B to ask a question that makes the player think harder — using their actual numbers — required more prompt engineering than any other part of the system. WebSocket streaming on free HuggingFace infrastructure introduced a batching bug that required bypassing React's state update mechanism entirely.
caseStudy.myRole: Everything — simulation engine design, RAG architecture and knowledge base authoring, Fastify gateway, WebSocket streaming layer, conflict detector, archetype system, React frontend, cross-domain auth, and deployment.
responsibilities: Designed and built the full simulation engine: 8 policy levers mapping to 10 outcome metrics (GDP growth, inflation, unemployment, debt-to-GDP, currency strength, trade balance, innovation index, real salaries, citizen mood, sovereign fund growth) across 7–8 rounds

Authored 99 game-situated RAG knowledge chunks across 5 layers: game mechanics, dangerous policy combinations, crisis playbooks, round strategy, and historical analogies (Weimar, Volcker, Singapore, Zimbabwe) — each written as a game-aware assertion, not a textbook fact
Built the full RAG pipeline: game state embedding → pgvector retrieval in Supabase → prompt construction with retrieved context → Llama 3.3 70B via Groq streaming over WebSocket

Built a pure-Python conflict detector that flags dangerous policy pairs (money printing into high inflation, rate cuts with a weak currency) before any LLM call — faster, cheaper, and more reliable than model inference

Engineered the Fastify gateway: same-domain cookie proxying for browser sessions, JWT in WebSocket URL for streaming connections, LRU caching keyed by state hash and prompt version, request queuing across two HuggingFace Spaces per service

Fixed a WebSocket streaming bug where tokens arriving within the same millisecond collapsed React's batch buffer — solved by accumulating tokens directly into the messages array via an index ref, bypassing React's batching entirely
Designed a 7-archetype classification system running at zero inference cost using pure logic priority checks, and an AI-narrated mandate timeline that reviews every policy choice at game end
approach: Get the simulation loop working before anything else — one round of policy → consequence → metric update, end to end, before building the advisor or gamification

Write the RAG knowledge base as game-situated assertions rather than economic facts. The model doesn't know what EconoQuest is — the retrieved context tells it. Every chunk had to be specific enough to retrieve on a real game state, not general enough to match anything

Enforce the Socratic constraint via prompt structure, not model capability. A capable model wants to give answers; the prompt had to structurally prevent it while still letting the model use the player's actual numbers

Run domain expertise as code, not inference. The conflict detector catches the most dangerous policy pairs in pure Python before touching the LLM — cheaper, faster, and more deterministic than asking the model to notice the same thing

Use free infrastructure as a design constraint, not a limitation. LRU caching keyed by state hash, load balancing across two HuggingFace Spaces per service, and KV caching (why streaming is 5 seconds, not 35) are architectural decisions that emerged from the zero-budget constraint
technicalSolution: React frontend with WebSocket streaming — fixed a critical batching bug by accumulating tokens via index ref instead of setState, bypassing React's update coalescing for real-time stream rendering

Fastify gateway handles all cross-cutting concerns: cookie proxying, JWT issuance for WebSocket connections, LRU cache keyed by state hash + prompt version, request queuing, and load balancing across two HuggingFace Spaces per service
RAG pipeline: game state → embedding → pgvector retrieval in Supabase → context injection → Llama 3.3 70B via Groq → WebSocket stream to client. 99 chunks across 5 knowledge layers
Pure-Python conflict detector runs before every LLM call, flagging dangerous policy pairs using domain logic with zero token cost
7-archetype classification system determined by pure priority-order logic checks — zero inference cost, instant result
AI-narrated mandate timeline generated at game end: a full review of every policy choice across the entire run, not a score
Hall of Fame leaderboard ranking mandates by weighted score (economic performance × nation difficulty) to incentivize high-risk, high-reward play
caseStudy.architectureNotes: Three-tier architecture on free infrastructure. React frontend communicates with a Fastify gateway via HTTP (authenticated flows) and WebSocket (streaming advisory responses). The gateway handles auth (same-domain cookie proxying for the browser session, JWT-in-URL for the WebSocket connection), LRU caching keyed by state hash and prompt version, and load balancing across two HuggingFace Spaces per service. Advisory requests flow through the conflict detector first — pure Python, zero tokens — then into the RAG pipeline: game state is embedded, pgvector in Supabase retrieves the most relevant of 99 knowledge chunks, a situated prompt is constructed, and Llama 3.3 70B via Groq streams the response back over WebSocket. KV caching keeps the streaming latency at ~5 seconds rather than 35. The archetype system and mandate timeline run entirely client-side at game end with no additional inference cost.

outcomes.qualitative: Submitted to Hackonomics 2026 as a solo build — zero cloud spend, production-grade architecture. The Socratic advisor generates genuinely situated hints using real game state: players get told about Weimar Germany because their specific inflation and money supply figures matched that RAG chunk, not because it was a random example. The WebSocket streaming pipeline held under demo conditions. The conflict detector eliminated the most dangerous false-positive advisor hints without touching the LLM.

proofPoints: Full RAG pipeline shipped on zero cloud budget — HuggingFace Spaces, Supabase pgvector, Groq, all free tier.
99 game-situated knowledge chunks authored across 5 layers — each written as a specific game-aware assertion, not a textbook fact.
WebSocket streaming bug fixed by bypassing React's batching — tokens accumulate via index ref directly into the messages array.
Conflict detector runs in pure Python before every LLM call — domain expertise as deterministic logic, not inference.
Entire stack — gateway, RAG pipeline, simulation engine, frontend — built and deployed solo.
lessons: RAG chunk design determines advisor quality more than model capability. Writing chunks as game-situated assertions — specific to EconoQuest's mechanics, not macroeconomics in general — was the single highest-leverage design decision in the project.
Socratic prompting is harder to enforce than expected. A capable model defaults to helpfulness, which usually means giving the answer. Structural prompt constraints matter more than instructions.
Domain expertise as code beats domain expertise as inference. The conflict detector is faster, cheaper, and more reliable than asking the model to notice dangerous policy pairs on its own.

Free infrastructure constraints produce better architecture. LRU caching, load balancing across Spaces, and KV cache utilization are patterns that scale — they emerged from a zero-budget constraint and would survive a paid infrastructure migration unchanged.

Streaming bugs are invisible until demo day. React's state batching collapsing a WebSocket stream produces silence — no error, no crash, just nothing rendering. Fix the stream first, then build the UI around it.
caseStudy.callToAction: Want to see the full RAG pipeline and simulation engine in action, or discuss production AI advisory systems built on free infrastructure? Try the live demo or reach out directly.

title: EcoLens — AI Waste Classifier
short: Point your camera at any waste item and instantly get an AI classification, real environmental impact data, and points toward a global leaderboard — turning recycling from a one-off action into a measurable habit.
problem: People want to recycle but don't know what goes where or how much their small actions actually matter. The gap between awareness and action is a UX problem as much as an information problem.
process: Designed the core loop: Identify → Quantify → Reward — so every scan produces a visible, cumulative result
Built a serverless Next.js backend that proxies image predictions through a HuggingFace-hosted ML model
Implemented a custom achievements engine with material-specific badges and a global leaderboard
Engineered an OTP-based auth system with JWT in HTTP-only cookies and token rotation
Applied conservative environmental impact formulas (CO₂, water, energy) tied to confidence scores and estimated weight
Iterated mobile camera and upload flows through multiple rounds to reduce UX friction
outcome: Placed 3rd out of 775 international participants at Hack for Humanity 2026 — built entirely solo. Delivered a production-grade app with a real ML pipeline, gamified engagement system, and robust auth — not a prototype.

stats.build: Solo — design, ML integration, backend, frontend, deployment

caseStudy.tlDr: Built and shipped an AI-powered waste classification app solo in one month — placed 3rd internationally at Hack for Humanity 2026 out of 775 participants. EcoLens turns a photo of any waste item into an AI label, estimated CO₂/water/energy impact, and gamified points — bridging the gap between environmental awareness and measurable daily action.
caseStudy.problem: Most people want to recycle responsibly but face two blockers: they don't know what material something is, and they have no sense of whether their effort matters at scale. Existing recycling apps either give dry information with no feedback loop, or require manual input. EcoLens was built to solve both: real-time AI classification plus cumulative impact that compounds over time.
caseStudy.constraints: One-month hackathon window, solo build, no budget for paid ML APIs, and a requirement to ship a judge-ready product — not a demo. Weight estimation from a 2D image, label ambiguity from the model, and auth reliability under edge cases were the hardest technical constraints.
caseStudy.myRole: Everything — product design, ML integration, backend architecture, frontend, auth system, achievements engine, deployment, and the submission video.

judgeScores.source: Official post-event results · Hack for Humanity 2026

responsibilities: Designed and built the full prediction pipeline: client image → POST /api/predict → HuggingFace proxy → label normalization → point & impact calculation → MongoDB write → frontend update
Built a custom achievements engine with material-specific badges (plastic, paper, glass, metal, organic) and a global leaderboard with real-time rank updates
Engineered OTP-based email verification with SMTP, JWT auth in HTTP-only cookies, and token rotation in /api/user — including transactional user creation with rollback on email failure
Implemented conservative environmental impact formulas: CO₂ = (estimated_weight_g / 1000) × EF_kg/tonne, with parallel calculations for water saved and energy saved
Handled low-confidence scan suppression — scans returning 'unknown' or below confidence threshold are not logged, keeping impact data honest

Designed a responsive UI with camera and upload flows, a lifetime impact dashboard, and Framer Motion animations — then iterated mobile UX through multiple rounds to reduce permission and cropping friction
approach: Started with the core loop first — get one scan working end-to-end before building any gamification
Chose HuggingFace Spaces for the ML endpoint to stay within zero budget with no cold-start penalty
Kept impact math conservative and transparent — approximate weight ranges per category, documented multipliers, no inflated numbers
Built auth last but made it robust: OTP + JWT + token rotation + transactional rollback — the kind of detail that breaks apps at demo time
Submitted a structured video covering the problem, live demo, and architecture overview — knowing presentation is scored equally alongside code
technicalSolution: Next.js (App Router) for the full stack — serverless API routes handle prediction proxy, auth, achievements, and leaderboard
HuggingFace Space hosts the image classification model; results are proxied server-side to normalize labels and strip raw confidence scores from the client
MongoDB stores users, scan history, achievement state, and leaderboard rankings — Mongoose handles schema validation and transactional user creation
JWT in HTTP-only cookies with token rotation on every /api/user call — SMTP OTP for email verification via Nodemailer
SWR for client-side data fetching — dashboard and leaderboard update reactively without full page reloads
Framer Motion for scan result animations, badge unlocks, and dashboard entrance sequences
Tailwind for consistent, responsive UI across camera, upload, dashboard, and leaderboard views
caseStudy.architectureNotes: Fully serverless within Next.js — no separate backend process. Client sends a base64 image to POST /api/predict. The route proxies to the HuggingFace endpoint, receives labels + confidence scores, maps the top label to one of six categories (plastic, paper, glass, metal, organic, other), computes points and impact using estimated weight ranges per category, writes the scan to MongoDB, updates the user's cumulative stats and achievement state, then returns the enriched result to the client in a single response. Low-confidence results and 'unknown' labels are rejected before the write step — keeping impact data honest. Auth is handled via /api/user: OTP is generated and emailed on registration, verified on the next call, and a JWT is issued into an HTTP-only cookie with rotation on every subsequent authenticated request.

outcomes.qualitative: Placed 3rd internationally at Hack for Humanity 2026 — solo build, 775 participants. Judges scored the project on impact, innovation, design, and presentation. The predict → persist → notify pipeline held up under demo conditions, auth edge cases were handled, and the leaderboard and achievements gave the project a live, working feel rather than a static prototype.

proofPoints: 3rd place finish at Hack for Humanity 2026 — 775 international participants, solo build.
Full ML pipeline shipped within a 1-month hackathon window with zero paid API budget.
Auth system handles OTP verification, JWT rotation, and transactional rollback — no auth failures during judging.
Conservative impact formulas with confidence-gated scan logging — data integrity over inflated numbers.
lessons: Integrating ML is more than wiring up a model — UX around low confidence, error states, and mobile camera flows determines whether the product feels real or broken.
Small auth details (cookie naming consistency, token rotation, OTP edge cases) break apps more reliably than mis-tuned models. Get auth right before building features on top of it.
Conservative math builds more trust than impressive-looking numbers. Judges and users both notice when impact estimates feel inflated.
Gamification works — the leaderboard and badges gave the project energy during the demo that a plain scan tool would not have had.
Presentation is half the score. A clear problem statement, live demo, and architecture walkthrough in the video matter as much as the code.
